definitions.explanation: An extremely small piece or particle. Often used in cooking to describe finely chopped ingredients (みじん{切|ぎ}り).

definitions.gloss: the slightest bit; not at all (in negative expressions)
definitions.explanation: Used with negative expressions to emphasize the complete absence of something — not even the tiniest amount.

examples.japanese: {玉|たま}ねぎを{微塵|みじん}{切|ぎ}りにする。
にんにくを{微塵|みじん}{切|ぎ}りにして{炒|いた}める。
examples.english: Mince the garlic and stir-fry it.

examples.japanese: {花瓶|かびん}が{落|お}ちて{微塵|みじん}に{砕|くだ}けた。
examples.english: The vase fell and shattered into tiny pieces.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}には{反省|はんせい}の{色|いろ}が{微塵|みじん}もない。
examples.english: He doesn't show the slightest sign of remorse.

examples.japanese: そんなこと{微塵|みじん}も{思|おも}わなかった。
examples.english: I didn't think that at all.

examples.japanese: {疑|うたが}いの{気持|きも}ちは{微塵|みじん}もなく、{彼女|かのじょ}を{完全|かんぜん}に{信|しん}じていた。
examples.english: Without the slightest doubt, I completely trusted her.

notes:
USAGE:
Two main uses: (1) In cooking, {微塵|みじん}{切|ぎ}り means finely minced or diced. (2) In the pattern {微塵|みじん}も〜ない, it emphasizes the complete absence of something. Both uses are very common.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {微塵|みじん}{切|ぎ}り (mincing, finely diced)
- {微塵|みじん}も〜ない (not the slightest ~)
- {微塵|みじん}に{砕|くだ}ける (to shatter into fragments)
- {微塵|みじん}も{感|かん}じない (not to feel in the slightest)
